```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)
library(fivethirtyeight)
library(data.table)

candy <- fivethirtyeight::candy_rankings 

candy <- candy |> 
  mutate(type = case_when(
    chocolate & fruity ~ "both",
    chocolate ~ "chocolate",
    fruity ~ "fruity",
    .default = "other"
  ))

```

# Fruity or Chocolaty?

## Row 1 {height="15%"}

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total Candies"

list(
  icon = "basket", 
  color = "warning", 
  value = nrow(candy))

```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Number of Fruity Candies"


list(
  icon = "heart-fill",
  color = "#E4572E",
  value = sum(candy$type == "fruity"))

```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Number of Chocolate Candies"

list(
  icon = "heart",
  color = "#7B4B2A",
  value = sum(candy$type == "chocolate"))
```

#### Research Question

Does more sugar mean these candies are more popular?

This dashboard explores the relationship between sugar content and candy popularity using the FiveThirtyEight candy rankings dataset. The scatterplot and regression line visualizations will help identify whether candies with higher sugar content tend to receive higher popularity scores among consumers.

# Win %

```{r}
boxplot <- ggplot(candy, aes(type, winpercent, color = type, fill = type)) + 
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.15, width = 0.55, outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(y = "Win %",
       x = "Candy Type")

ggplotly(boxplot)
```

# Win % of Candies

```{r}
bar <- ggplot(candy, aes(winpercent, reorder(competitorname, winpercent), fill = type)) +
  geom_col() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 4)) +
  labs(y = "Candy Name",
       x = "Win %")

ggplotly(bar)
```

```{r}
candy <- candy |>
  select(competitorname, sugarpercent, winpercent) |>
  drop_na() |>
  arrange(desc(sugarpercent))

most_sugar <- candy |>
  slice_max(sugarpercent, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

least_sugar <- candy |>
  slice_min(sugarpercent, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

average_popularity <- mean(candy$winpercent)
```

# Candy Popularity

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Most Sugary Candy"
#| color: danger

list(
  icon = "candy-cane",
  value = most_sugar$competitorname,
  caption = paste0(
    round(most_sugar$sugarpercent * 100, 1),
    "% sugar"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Least Sugary Candy"
#| color: success

list(
  icon = "leaf",
  value = least_sugar$competitorname,
  caption = paste0(
    round(least_sugar$sugarpercent * 100, 1),
    "% sugar"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Average Popularity"
#| color: primary

list(icon = "chart-line", 
     value = paste0(round(average_popularity, 1), "%"),
     caption = "Average candy popularity score")
```

# Popularity

```{r}
#| title: "Is more sugar more popular?"
#| fig-height: 6

sugar_plot <- ggplot(candy,aes(x = sugarpercent, y = winpercent, 
                               text = paste0("Candy: ", competitorname,
                                             "<br>Sugar: ", round(sugarpercent * 100, 1), 
                                             "%",
                                             "<br>Popularity: ", round(winpercent, 1), "%"))) +
  geom_point(color = "#00B8D9", size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#FF8C42", fill = "#FF8C42", alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(x = "Sugar Percentage", y = "Popularity Score (%)", 
       title = "Does More Sugar Mean More Popular?") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggplotly(sugar_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

# Candy Dataframe

```{r}
#| title: "Candy Rankings Data"

candy <- fivethirtyeight::candy_rankings 

candy |> 
  select(c(competitorname, hard, bar, sugarpercent)) 

knitr::kable(candy)
```
